extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers invited to review manuscripts for Sage journals using the Sage Track (ScholarOne) system
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural standards for completing peer reviews in Sage's ScholarOne-branded Sage Track submission and review system, including account setup, responding to invitations, submitting reviews, and maintaining reviewer availability. Focused on practical steps reviewers must follow when using the online system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account creation / login per journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Every journal’s Sage Track site requires a separate account and login; an account for one journal will not transfer to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invited to review, an account will already have been created for you — follow the link in the invitation email. For new accounts, see Silverchair reviewer support (reviewer guide). It is recommended to use ORCID login to streamline the process; if you use ORCID you will be able to login with ORCID for each journal site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to invitation (accept/decline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invitation email contains title and abstract and options to accept or decline the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The easiest way to respond is by selecting the appropriate link within the invitation email. You can also log into your Sage Track account, locate open invitations, and select your response under the 'Action' dropdown. If unable to review, provide suggestions for suitable alternate reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review turnaround expectation: on average, journals ask reviewers to return their comments in two to three weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the deadline displayed in the Review page. If you cannot meet the deadline, decline promptly and suggest alternates so the editorial process is not delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide substitute reviewer suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are unable to review the manuscript, suggest suitable alternate reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors appreciate suggested alternatives to speed selection; include contact details and any relevant conflicts of interest when proposing alternates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing manuscript and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Reviewer Center / Review page to view the PDF or HTML of the manuscript, the abstract, deadlines, and (for revisions) the author’s response if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Reviewer Center dashboard shows current reviews, submitted reviews, and open invitations. Use these tools to locate files and important metadata (e.g., deadlines, editor contact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting review and recommending a decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Within Sage Track you will have the opportunity to provide comments and recommend a decision to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete any structured review fields (ratings, checklist items) and provide an overall recommendation where requested. Follow journal-specific instructions displayed in the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of comments: author vs editor
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments directed to the author must be located under 'Comments to the Author' and all confidential comments to the editor under 'Confidential Comments to the Editor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting, ensure you have entered comments in the correct fields; do not put confidential remarks meant for the editor in the author-facing box. Many journals allow both types of comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete all required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: All required fields (marked with red asterisks) must be completed before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the form for required entries and any mandatory ratings or textual responses. The system will typically prevent submission until required fields are filled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to COPE guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your review follows COPE (Committee on Publication Ethics) guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should follow ethical guidance on confidentiality, conflicts of interest, and professional conduct as set out by COPE. If unsure about ethical issues, contact the editor or consult COPE resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available help resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For technical help using Sage Track, consult the Silverchair reviewer support page which includes video tutorials and FAQs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions about journal-specific reviewer expectations, contact the journal's editor or administrator. Use the support materials to resolve navigation or upload issues before contacting staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when journal lacks online system
rubrics_metrics.description: If the journal you're reviewing for doesn't use an online submission system, follow instructions in your invitation email and email your comments directly to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully review invitation instructions to ensure correct submission format; reach out to the editor if you have questions about how to submit or format your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep availability updated
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should update their availability regularly in Sage Track to avoid being invited when unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log into the journal’s Sage Track site, click your name in the blue banner, select 'User ID & Password', scroll to 'Unavailable Dates', set 'From' and 'To' using the calendar buttons, include the reason for unavailability, and click 'Finish' to save. This helps Editorial Office selection.
